text:
monica: Quick sync after the midnight canary. Small cohort saw p95 jumps when hosts drained; looks like cold KV + routing jitter.
ryan: how big was the impact?
monica: ~3% of requests, p95 ~1.6x for ~10m. Not catastrophic but raised alarms for the dashboard.
jia: idea: conservative handoff that minimizes user-impact. three levers: tokenized grace for active sessions, rate-limited prefetch (no full-route probes), and an SLO-credit counter that gates commit.
ryan: explain SLO-credit?
jia: each rollout gets a small bank of credits. Handoff operations that cause extra latency consume credits; if credits fall below threshold we auto-stop and fallback. prevents silent degradation.
monica: config sketch we can include in RFC (stored as strings in proto): {"mode":"conservative-handoff","grace_tokens":"1","prefetch_rate_pct":"2","slo_credit_budget":"200","fallback_p95_ratio":"1.5"}
sam: sticky sessions remain on source until end by default. Grace-tokens let very active sessions continue for short TTL while targets warm.
ryan: telemetry needed: token-usage, prefetch_hit_rate, slo_credit_remaining, per-cohort p95_ratio, and last-fallback-reason. Console panels + an alert when slo_credit_remaining < 10%.
monica: runbook: on fallback event check recent drains, token usage, prefetch_hit trend. Steps: 1) pause rollout, 2) top-up small credits if safe, 3) increase prefetch_rate up to max, 4) rollback if no recovery in X minutes.
jia: testing: unit transitions, simulator sweep thresholds, canary with synthetic long-session workload, chaos test injecting KV delays.
infra-bot: scheduled-canary: job 2024-04-20T01:00Z created for variant v2; will emit handoff/fallback events.
monica: I'll draft RFC + sample runbook and include the config proto and sim results. Ping eng-oncall for first 48h after rollout. :thumbsup:
